# Install Paneflow on Linux

> Install Paneflow on Linux with AppImage, .deb, .rpm, or .tar.gz. Choose a package for x86_64 or ARM64, check Vulkan requirements, and resolve FUSE or PATH errors.

Canonical: https://paneflow.dev/docs/installation/linux

<!-- Auto-generated mirror of paneflow.dev - do not edit by hand.
     Source of truth: the paneflow.dev docs. Regenerated by
     scripts/sync-public-docs.ts in the site repo. -->

Paneflow provides Linux packages for `x86_64` and ARM64 (`aarch64`).
Choose the format for your distribution below. You do not need Rust or
build tools to install these packages.

## Choose an installation format

| Distribution or installation type | Format | Updates |
|---|---|---|
| Ubuntu, Debian | `.deb` | Through `apt` after the first install |
| Fedora, openSUSE | `.rpm` | Through `dnf` or `zypper` after the first install |
| Run a downloaded file without a system package | AppImage | In-app updater |
| Arch or an installation in your home directory | `.tar.gz` | In-app updater or install a newer archive |

Paneflow needs a graphical session and a GPU driver that supports Vulkan.
The `.deb` and `.rpm` packages declare the required system libraries,
but you still need a working GPU driver. For AppImage and `.tar.gz`
installs, check that the Vulkan loader is installed: `libvulkan1` on
Debian and Ubuntu, `vulkan-loader` on Fedora, or `vulkan-icd-loader` on Arch.
For graphics errors, follow the [Vulkan troubleshooting guide](/docs/troubleshooting).

Run the download and installation commands in **Bash**, with `curl`
installed, from the folder where you want to download the package.
Each download block detects your processor architecture and fetches the
latest release. Choose one format; you do not need to install all four.

## How do I install Paneflow as an AppImage?

Use the AppImage to run Paneflow without installing a system package or
using `sudo`. Download the file, make it executable, and launch it:

```bash
ARCH="$(uname -m)"
[ "$ARCH" = "arm64" ] && ARCH="aarch64"
VERSION="$(curl -fsSL https://api.github.com/repos/arthjean/paneflow/releases/latest | sed -nE 's/.*"tag_name": "v([^"]+)".*/\1/p')"
curl -fLO "https://github.com/arthjean/paneflow/releases/download/v${VERSION}/paneflow-${VERSION}-${ARCH}.AppImage"
chmod +x "paneflow-${VERSION}-${ARCH}.AppImage"
./"paneflow-${VERSION}-${ARCH}.AppImage"
```

If startup fails with `dlopen(): error loading libfuse.so.2`, run the
AppImage without FUSE:

```bash
./"paneflow-${VERSION}-${ARCH}.AppImage" --appimage-extract-and-run
```

On Ubuntu 24.04, you can install the FUSE 2 library with
`sudo apt install libfuse2t64`, then launch the AppImage normally.
See the [AppImage FUSE instructions](https://docs.appimage.org/user-guide/troubleshooting/fuse.html)
for other distributions.

To use the `paneflow` command, move the AppImage into `~/.local/bin` and
rename it to `paneflow`:

```bash
mkdir -p ~/.local/bin
mv "paneflow-${VERSION}-${ARCH}.AppImage" ~/.local/bin/paneflow
chmod +x ~/.local/bin/paneflow
```

If your shell cannot find the command, follow the PATH instructions below.
If you still need to run without FUSE after moving the file, use
`~/.local/bin/paneflow --appimage-extract-and-run`.
Paneflow stores its settings and workspace state in `~/.paneflow` by
default, separately from the AppImage. See the [configuration guide](/docs/configuration).

## How do I install Paneflow on Ubuntu or Debian?

Download the `.deb` for your processor and install it with `apt`:

```bash
DEB_ARCH="$(dpkg --print-architecture)"
case "$DEB_ARCH" in
  amd64) ARCH="x86_64" ;;
  arm64) ARCH="aarch64" ;;
  *) echo "Unsupported architecture: $DEB_ARCH" >&2; exit 1 ;;
esac
VERSION="$(curl -fsSL https://api.github.com/repos/arthjean/paneflow/releases/latest | sed -nE 's/.*"tag_name": "v([^"]+)".*/\1/p')"
curl -fLO "https://github.com/arthjean/paneflow/releases/download/v${VERSION}/paneflow-${VERSION}-${ARCH}.deb"
sudo apt install "./paneflow-${VERSION}-${ARCH}.deb"
```

The package installs `paneflow` at `/usr/bin/paneflow` and registers the
Paneflow package repository. For later updates, run `sudo apt update`,
then `sudo apt upgrade paneflow`.

To uninstall, run `sudo apt remove paneflow`. Use `sudo apt purge paneflow`
to also remove the Paneflow repository entry and signing key.

## How do I install Paneflow on Fedora or openSUSE?

Download the `.rpm` for your processor. On Fedora, install it with `dnf`.
On openSUSE, replace the final installation line as shown below before
running the block:

```bash
ARCH="$(uname -m)"
[ "$ARCH" = "arm64" ] && ARCH="aarch64"
VERSION="$(curl -fsSL https://api.github.com/repos/arthjean/paneflow/releases/latest | sed -nE 's/.*"tag_name": "v([^"]+)".*/\1/p')"
curl -fLO "https://github.com/arthjean/paneflow/releases/download/v${VERSION}/paneflow-${VERSION}-${ARCH}.rpm"
sudo dnf install "./paneflow-${VERSION}-${ARCH}.rpm"
```

On openSUSE, replace the final `sudo dnf install` line with:

```bash
sudo zypper install "./paneflow-${VERSION}-${ARCH}.rpm"
```

The package registers the Paneflow RPM repository. For later updates,
use `sudo dnf upgrade paneflow` on Fedora or `sudo zypper update paneflow`
on openSUSE.

## How do I install Paneflow from a tarball?

Use the `.tar.gz` archive for an installation in your home directory,
including on Arch. Download and extract it, then run the included installer:

```bash
ARCH="$(uname -m)"
[ "$ARCH" = "arm64" ] && ARCH="aarch64"
VERSION="$(curl -fsSL https://api.github.com/repos/arthjean/paneflow/releases/latest | sed -nE 's/.*"tag_name": "v([^"]+)".*/\1/p')"
curl -fLO "https://github.com/arthjean/paneflow/releases/download/v${VERSION}/paneflow-${VERSION}-${ARCH}.tar.gz"
tar -xzf "paneflow-${VERSION}-${ARCH}.tar.gz"
cd paneflow.app
./install.sh
```

The installer copies the app to `~/.local/paneflow.app`, creates the
`~/.local/bin/paneflow` symlink, and adds the application launcher and
icons under `~/.local/share`. Run it without `sudo`.

## How do I verify the installation?

Open a terminal and run:

```bash
paneflow --version
paneflow
```

The first command should print the installed version. The second should
open the Paneflow window. If the command is not found, follow the PATH
instructions below. If the window does not open, follow the
[launch and graphics troubleshooting guide](/docs/troubleshooting).

Once Paneflow opens, use the [getting started guide](/docs) to launch your
first agent. Install CLI agents separately and follow their sign-in instructions.

## What if `paneflow` is not found in my PATH?

The steps below apply to AppImage and `.tar.gz` installs. For a `.deb` or
`.rpm` install, open a new terminal and run `/usr/bin/paneflow --version`.
If that file is missing, reinstall the package.

If your shell reports `command not found`, first check that the file or
symlink exists with `ls -l ~/.local/bin/paneflow`. If it is missing, repeat
the AppImage move step or the `.tar.gz` installation above.

If the file exists but the command is not found, add `~/.local/bin` to
your shell's `PATH`. Run only the block for the shell you use, once:

**Bash** (`~/.bashrc`):

```bash
echo 'export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"' >> ~/.bashrc
source ~/.bashrc
```

**Zsh** (`~/.zshrc`):

```bash
echo 'export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"' >> ~/.zshrc
source ~/.zshrc
```

**Fish** (`~/.config/fish/config.fish`):

```fish
fish_add_path ~/.local/bin
```

Open a new terminal and run `paneflow --version` again. If it still fails,
consult the [PATH troubleshooting guide](/docs/troubleshooting).
